label: Inert emptiness from two grounding principles
description: New non-transcription conditional support option for premise A2 (inert emptiness) of Arrival A, composed from nothingFromNothing and inertOfNothingFromNothing. In a history with a concrete-empty moment s and a concrete thing x present at a later t, x is absent at s, so it began and has a concrete ground present at s or later; following such grounds through things that come to be after s, along a well-founded chain, ends at a concrete thing present at s, contradicting emptiness. Both premises are OPEN framework inputs about every history of the model; each is needed (controls 1 to 3). Together they carry no modal content (control 4); in Arrival A, necessity arises from A2 jointly with the possible contingent-free past, presence-to-existence and the frame premises. The premises are not shown to be better warranted than A2; they make its warrant explicit as a causal principle for beginnings with a presence clause and a well-foundedness condition confined to what comes to be after one moment. Nothing is attributed to a source. No premise truth is established.
